talks.title: The OSTRWERK Initiative
talks.teaser: Introduces the OSTRWERK open-source hardware initiative providing accessible RF tooling and equipment for amateur radio operators.
talks.summary:
In this practical hardware presentation from the DEF CON Safe Mode Ham Radio Village, a radio amateur introduces the OSTRWERK Initiative, designing rugged, field-deployable radio communication kits for disaster response. Opening at 00:04, the speaker reviews the technical requirements for portable communication stations capable of operating during extended power grid failures.

At 11:01, the presenter examines field station architectures, demonstrating custom Pelican-style waterproof cases integrating VHF/UHF transceivers, lithium iron phosphate battery management systems, and antenna tuners.

At 22:04 and 33:02, the speaker conducts a hardware demonstration, evaluating audio interface wiring between transceivers and Raspberry Pi single-board computers while discussing enclosure thermal management and magnetic keyboard mounting for portable digital emergency operations. talks.title: What Makes a Good Operator
talks.teaser: Experienced amateur radio operators discuss essential operational discipline, on-air etiquette, and community mentoring.
talks.summary:
Amateur radio operators Eric (AI0J), Justin (KE8MYF), Grant (W4K), and Richard (VA7OG) host a panel discussion in the Ham Radio Village on on-air operating ethics, radio etiquette, and community culture [01:54, 02:19].

The panelists demystify amateur radio jargon, Q-codes, and historical operating habits, discussing the balance between preserving telecommunications heritage and making on-air nets welcoming to newcomers [02:08, 19:05]. They share practical advice on concise emergency traffic handling during disaster spotter nets [19:07], resolving neighborhood antenna placement restrictions [25:04], and adopting modern digital voice modes such as Digital Mobile Radio (DMR) alongside traditional analog repeaters [30:37].

talks.title: Single Board Computers in Amateur Radio
talks.teaser: Demonstrates deploying Raspberry Pi and single-board computers for digital amateur radio modes, APRS gateways, and remote control.
talks.summary:
In this hardware tutorial from the DEF CON Safe Mode Ham Radio Village, an amateur radio operator demonstrates integrating Single Board Computers (SBCs) into modern ham radio stations. Opening at 00:02, the presenter compares popular SBC platforms, detailing the hardware specifications and power requirements of the Raspberry Pi 3B+ and Raspberry Pi 4.

At 11:00 and 22:00, the speaker walks through flashing headless Raspberry Pi OS images, configuring wpa_supplicant.conf for automated Wi-Fi provisioning, and configuring remote VNC access.

At 33:01 and 44:00, the demonstration illustrates interfacing the Raspberry Pi with an Icom transceiver via USB sound cards and CI-V rig control cables, configuring amateur radio software packages such as WSJT-X and FLDIGI to operate FT8 and digital packet modes in portable field environments. talks.title: The K0BAK News Van: Part 1
talks.teaser: Pete (K0BAK) details the conversion of a retired television news live broadcast van into a high-powered mobile amateur radio operations vehicle and field station.
talks.summary:
Repurposing Broadcast Vehicles for Mobile Radio

Retired television news broadcast vans offer robust chassis, integrated pneumatic masts, and isolated power systems ideal for heavy mobile amateur radio and emergency communications.

Pneumatic Mast and RF Antenna Mast Architecture

Pete (K0BAK) examines the mechanical restoration of the van's telescoping pneumatic antenna mast, detailing compressor controls, safety interlocks, and coaxial cabling harnesses.

Mobile Power Generation and Battery Banks

The speaker details rewiring the onboard commercial generator and DC battery banks to ensure clean, isolated, and sustained electrical power for high-wattage HF/VHF/UHF transceivers.

Operating a Mobile Field Communications Hub

The presentation demonstrates the completed internal operating console, field radio racks, and mobile deployment workflows for emergency communication drills.

talks.title: The K0BAK News Van: Part 2
talks.teaser: Walks through the mobile RF installation, power distribution, and antenna arrays in a converted news broadcast van.
talks.summary:
Amateur radio operator Pete (K0BAK) hosts an interactive technical Q&A in the Ham Radio Village, detailing his ambitious ongoing project to convert a decommissioned broadcast television news truck into a self-contained mobile emergency communications center [00:07, 00:17].

Pete answers community questions regarding vehicle logistics, chassis weight distribution, power generation, and RF antenna mast deployment [02:42, 04:55]. He walks through interior equipment rack layout, explaining cable management, equipment airflow, rear maintenance access [07:04], and physical security considerations when transporting high-frequency transceivers and repeater gear to remote operational sites [09:12].
